thread.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Undervalued According To DCF Analysis - Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. (NYSE:TSM)

author: Quintus Research
title: Taiwan Semiconductor Undervalued According To DCF Analysis - Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. (NYSE:TSM)

organizations.name: dcf analysis - taiwan semiconductor manufacturing company ltd.

text:
Introduction According to my discount cash flow analysis, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company's (NYSE: TSM ) intrinsic value is around $40 USD. The unlevered cash flow is expected to reach 371 million TWD in 2028 and grow at 3% in perpetuity (the conversion rate from TWD to USD is approximately 30 to 1).
The results are shown below.
(Source: Company annual filing , Model analysis)
For the discount rate, I have used a WACC = 7.9%, calculated using a CAPM model.
Since TSMC is a relatively mature company and already manufacturing at large scale, I believe the room for improvement in free cash flow from the operation side is rather limited. Therefore, I believe the critical component in determining TSMC's future cash flows is the revenue it will generate in the future.
Revenue Analysis and Forecasting I have modeled TSMC's revenue growth in the next 10 years to slow down to 2.1% with very conservative assumptions.
TSMC's business consists of four revenue-generating components, with communication being the largest, making up 60% of the total revenue.
(Source: Company annual filing )
Below is a description of each of the revenue segment taken from TSMC's annual SEC filings:
Communication: Semiconductors for communication applications are primarily used in mobile devices (including smartphone), wireless infrastructure and wireline infrastructure. Communication semiconductor products include, among others, baseband processor, application processor, radio-frequency IC, image sensor, small panel driver, fingerprint sensor, connectivity IC, network processor and ethernet switch. Computer: Semiconductors for computer applications are mainly used in personal computers and servers. Computer semiconductor products include, among others, central processing units (CPU), graphic processing units (GPUs), hard disk drive controller and application specific integrated circuits (“ASICs”) for machine learning, blockchain, and cryptocurrency mining. Consumer: Semiconductors for consumer applications are used in various consumer electronics, such as digital televisions, set-top-boxes, digital cameras and game consoles. Consumer semiconductor products include, among others, application specific standard product (ASSP) for digital televisions, set-top-boxes, digital cameras, and game consoles. Industrial /Standard : Semiconductors for industrial/standard applications are used in a wide range of end systems. Industrial/standard semiconductor products include, among others, micro controller units (MCU), power management IC, data converters, programmable logic devices (NYSE: PLD ) and flash controllers. I have modeled the growth of each segment based on their fundamental drivers.
Communication Segment Revenue Forecast
TSMC communication revenue = Total smartphones shipped x TSMC market share x Revenue per smartphone for TSMC
Since TSMC's market share already is near 55% (Source: Trendforce ), and the price of components inside smartphones have stabilized, I believe the main driver for this revenue segment is the shipment of smartphones in the future.
(Source: Statista )
I have consulted global smartphone shipment forecasts from Statista, and by the looks of it, global shipments of smartphones will stabilize around 1.6 to 1.7 billion units after 2022.
Beyond 2022, I have assumed the shipments to stay constant. This is a very conservative assumption because smartphone shipments will most likely continue to grow because the penetration rate is still very low in many countries. Take China, for example, the penetration rate is only 55% (calculated as smartphone users divided by online population) as of May 2018 (Not shown in the table below).
Smartphone penetration rate by country: (Source: Wikipedia )
Computer Segment Revenue Forecast
TSMC's Computer Segment consists of two major components, the PC market and the Data Center market. PC shipment and average price is driven by consumer spending, and has stabilized or even decreased over the past few years.
Gartner Says Worldwide PC Shipments Declined 1.4 Percent in First Quarter of 2018 (Source: Gartner ).
However, the Data Center market has been growing relatively fast for the past few quarters. This is driven by companies beginning to adopt cloud technology and as Internet users continue to grow and generate more data. I would expect data center expansion to be the major driver for this revenue segment for the future.
According to IDC:
"Worldwide Server Market Revenue Grew 43.7% Year Over Year to a Record $22.5 Billion During the Second Quarter of 2018, According to IDC" (Source: IDC ).
43.7% growth rate is very impressive. Even though this growth rate is most likely to decline in the near future, I believe the growth trend will continue for two reasons. The first is that, as I have mentioned above, traditional companies began to embrace cloud technology as a better alternative to local data servers. This is because cloud computing is less capital intensive and more flexible. The second reason is that new internet companies are still popping up across the world. Take TikTok, the latest popular consumer media app, for example. It already has more than 500 million monthly active users (MAU) as of July 2018 and is still growing fast (Source: SCMP.com ). To store all these newly generated data, more data centers are required.
(Source: Statista )
To forecast TSMC's computer revenue, I have used the following formula:
TSMC Computer Revenue = (PC Shipment x TSMC Market Share x TSMC Revenue per unit) + (Server Shipment x TSMC Market Share x TSMC Revenue per unit)
I have assumed TSMC's market share would be constant for the PC and Server market in the future to be conservative. However, it's likely that TSMC's market share would rise when AMD began to eat into Intel's market share (which I will discuss in more detail later in this article).
I have assumed PC shipments to stay constant in the future but the revenue per unit will increase at a rate of 1% due to inflation.
I also assumed server shipments to increase at 5% annually in the future. This is a very conservative assumption given that data center servers are growing at more than 40% YoY currently.
Consumer and Industrial/Standard Revenue Forecast
These two components are very hard to forecast since they include lots of miscellaneous parts. I have assumed a very conservative growth rate of 2% for the next 10 years for both of the segments. Again given that these two segments currently have 10%-15% CAGR, this assumption is reasonable.
Putting it all together, I have forecasted TSMC's total revenue to grow to 1.2 trillion TWD in 2028 with a CAGR of 2.1%. (Source: Company annual filing and model analysis)
TSMC Technological Advancement and Customer Base Analysis TSMC already has implemented 10nm technology in two of its Fabs and is beginning to utilize 7nm technology. This puts TSMC even ahead of Intel in terms of wafer density.
Side note: The lower the diameter of the die, the higher the density the wafer and thus the greater the production capacity and lower cost per unit, going from 12 to 10 is about 30% increase in density and (12*12 = 144; 10*10 = 100) and thus very significant.
We can see that the two Fabs opened in 2001 and 2012 already implemented 10nm technology on 12-inch wafers. Increasing density will not only increase TSMC's technological barrier to fend off competitors and new entrants but also will expand its manufacturing capacity, increasing its scale of economy. (Source: Company annual filing )
In addition, TSMC already has developed 7nm technology for the newest iPhone, securing its position as one of Apple's (NASDAQ: AAPL ) most important supplier for years to come.
(Source: VentureBeat.com)
Furthermore, being AMD's ( AMD ) major supplier, TSMC will benefit greatly as AMD begin to eat into Intel's ( INTC ) data server market share.
AMD's (NASDAQ: AMD ) new EYPC series of server chips are reported being more cost effective than Intel's (NASDAQ: INTC ) current server chips and may take away as much as 15%-20% of the server market share from Intel.
Intel has its own chipset fabs and therefore does not heavily rely on TSMC to produce its chipsets. However, AMD, only focused on chip design and does not have its on fabs, heavily relies on TSMC to manufacture its chipset, including its new EYPC series (Source: ExtremeTech ). As AMD eats into Intel's market share in the data center market, TSMC's computer segment revenue will likely grow even faster. In addition, AMD will help TSMC in developing manufacturing techniques for complex chipset structures to compete with Intel in the future.
We came away from a meeting with CEO Brian Krzanich last week believing that the burden is on (positive earnings) revisions to drive continued outperformance; we are less confident about further multiple expansion,” analyst Romit Shah said in a note to clients Monday. “Mr. Krzanich was very matter-of-fact in saying that Intel would lose server share to AMD in the second half of the year. This wasn’t new news, but we thought it was interesting that Mr. Krzanich did not draw a firm line in the sand as it relates to AMD’s potential gains in servers; he only indicated that it was Intel’s job to not let AMD capture 15-20% market share. ( Source: CNBC )
Outstanding Profit Margin and Healthy Balance Sheet Finally, TSMC's scale of economy and advancement in technology has transferred into an outstanding profit margin and a healthy balance sheet. This will put TSMC in a favorable position if an economic crisis happens.
During an economic crisis, cash is king. TSMC's has about $15 billion USD of cash on hand and close to zero debt. Its current debt/capital ratio is only about 10% with an Aa3 rating on its bonds. Therefore TSMC does not have to worry about refinancing its loans or the risk of rising interest rates.
Due to TSMC's outstanding profit margin of 35%, it's able to finance most of its capex using operating cash flow and does not need to raise additional debt. With all the cash, TSMC can increase its capex and R&D to further heighten its technological barrier or increase its current production capacity to fend off competitions, or it can use extra cash to increase dividends or repurchase shares.
(Source: Company annual filing)
Risks There are two major risks for investing in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. The most significant one is the deterioration of the current trade war between the U.S. and China. If this trade war continues for a long time in the future, it's likely to reduce the global demand for semiconductors and negatively impact TSMC's revenue. However, I believe my revenue growth assumptions already are very conservative and thus have taken part of the probability of this event happening into consideration. The second risk is the return on investment of 7nm technology being below expectation. If this happens, it may negatively impact TSMC's profit margin and constrain its free cash flow.
Conclusion Overall, taking all the risks into consideration, I believe TSMC's current market price is below its intrinsic value. The intrinsic value should be at least $40 using DCF analysis. The semiconductor industry is most likely to continue to grow as more people begin to develop a closer relationship to the Internet and technology. Owning a major player in this field at a reasonable price would add great value to the investment portfolio.
Disclosure: I am/we are long TSM.
